clue.text: Room 101's about coverage of Poles

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: An Orwellian nod to Room 101, the torture chamber of Nineteen Eighty-Four, oddly concerned with polar coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SPACECI round, giving IC + ECAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar regions are covered by permanent sheets of ice, so these are the coverings of the Poles.

clue.text: Former police upset reserves in cover

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Retired police officers are annoyed at reservists being kept under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RUC into CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a hanging piece of fabric that screens a window, a cover in the sense of a screen.

clue.text: Vessel made of tin and aluminium

parts.note: a tin is a can
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A container described as made of tin and aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a pot or ship; here it is a duct in the body, or a waterway that carries boats.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a canal is a tube-like duct, a vessel carrying fluid through the body.

clue.text: Erect border, forbidding one making the hajj?

indicators.note: in a down clue erect means set upright, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lip is a border or rim
forbidding means grim, stern-looking

explanation.surface: A stern fence is put up to keep out someone travelling to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erect' makes LIP read upwards as PIL. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a Muslim travelling to Mecca is one kind of religious traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The hajj is the Muslim journey to Mecca, so anyone undertaking it is a religious traveller to a holy site.

clue.text: Les abandons hopelessly bad security device

indicators.note: bad signals that the remaining letters are in a poor, jumbled order
abandons means the letters of Les leave the word that follows

explanation.surface: A man called Les gives up on a security gadget that is utterly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes LES out of HOPELESSLY, leaving HOPESLY, which 'bad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A peephole in a door lets the occupant see who is outside before opening it, a simple safety measure.

clue.text: Race former footballer after invasive surgery

indicators.note: invasive means pushing its way in, so the surgery goes inside the footballer's name

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A retired football star has to race after an invasive operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a verb about running; it is a noun meaning an ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a nation or ethnic group is a people, as in the peoples of Africa.

clue.text: Give service in court — carpentry, perhaps

parts.note: to hand is to give

indicators.note: in places the service within the court abbreviation

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Serving at tennis described alongside woodwork, as if a hobby list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' and 'court' look like tennis; service is the armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is one example of skilled manual work making things by hand.

clue.text: Fish cross river in UK, lying low

indicators.note: cross means go across, so the fish spans the inner letters, holding them inside

parts.note: the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

indicators.note: in places the river letter inside UK

explanation.surface: An angry fish swims across a British river and hides at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside UK making URK, and 'cross' has LING straddle it, L-URK-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is lurking is hiding out of sight, keeping a low profile.

clue.text: Pumping iron into great cast

indicators.note: cast means molded anew, so the letters are thrown into a fresh form, as iron is cast in a foundry

explanation.surface: Weightlifting in a gym, with iron poured into a mould by a foundryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pumping' suggests pumping iron at the gym; here it means questioning someone hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, so pumping is a grilling.

clue.text: Press group returning from Pakistan or India

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
group here means a cluster of consecutive letters taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper group coming home from the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Press group' as the definition, but only 'Press' defines; 'group' marks a run of letters inside 'Pakistan or India', and 'returning' reverses NORI.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat with a hot appliance, a verb synonym.

clue.text: City drugs impress northern people with their properties

indicators.note: impress means press inward, so the northern letter is pushed in between the other pieces

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the usual crossword city
downers are depressant drugs

explanation.surface: A city's drug problem makes a mark on northerners with their own homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners of estates and land are property holders, people with real estate to their names.

clue.text: Shadow old Republican worker in Savile Row

parts.note: to shadow someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A spy follows an elderly Republican politician who works on a smart London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is a street in London famous for bespoke men's suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row's shops are where gentlemen's suits are made to measure, so a craftsman there cuts cloth.

clue.text: Catholic Celtic played boring European clubs

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the rearranged team goes inside the other letters

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: played means performed in a fresh way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Celtic, the Glasgow football club with a Catholic following, play dull football against European sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' with a capital looks religious; it means wide-ranging. 'played' turns CELTIC into CLECTI, which 'boring' puts inside E...C. Celtic is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means broad and all-embracing in taste, which describes someone drawing from many sources.

clue.text: Modern husbandmen replacing area with old grasses

parts.note: in means fashionable or modern

indicators.note: replacing means the area letter is swapped out for the old letter

parts.note: husbandmen are farmers, those who till the land

explanation.surface: Contemporary farmers switching land over to old grass varieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasses' looks botanical; in British slang a grass is someone who informs to police. 'replacing' turns FARMERS into FORMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to grass on someone is to tell the police, so the grasses are snitches.

clue.text: Disallowed remaining game, then went in front

parts.note: over means left over, remaining
RU is rugby union
led means was in front, ahead

explanation.surface: A referee rules out a score in the remaining play after the side moved ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: When a decision is overturned or a goal ruled out by an official, it has been set aside.

clue.text: Called English sweep

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned an English chimney sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweep' looks like a chimney sweep; it is the noun for an extent or scope.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep of something is its full extent or scope, as in a broad span of view.

clue.text: Fan left deliveries at Old Trafford

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries; Old Trafford in Manchester is a Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: A supporter leaves after watching the bowling at Old Trafford, a Manchester sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is also Manchester United's football ground, but the cricket ground of the same name is meant: an over is six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast or devotee, as a music lover is.

clue.text: Busy place to start monopoly?

definitions.meaning: busy means constantly active, never resting
players of the board game Monopoly begin on the corner square marked GO

explanation.surface: Someone too occupied to play board games.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'monopoly' disguises the board game Monopoly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly active is an idiom for busy; in Monopoly every token sits on the starting square first.

clue.text: A soldier at Waterloo, say, heading off trouble

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: Waterloo is a London railway station

explanation.surface: An American soldier at Waterloo heading off to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterloo' suggests the battle; it is London's railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is disturbance or unrest, the state of being troubled or stirred up.

clue.text: Characteristic feature or mole

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: A distinctive feature on the skin, or a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like a skin blemish, fitting the facial surface; it is a spy inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy embedded within an organisation who betrays it from the inside.

clue.text: Watch old boy start game in court

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
in tennis each point starts with a serve

explanation.surface: A former pupil opens a tennis match on court.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully, a direct synonym for looking on.

clue.text: Leader of old kingdom leaves country

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the kingdom's name
leaves means that letter goes away

parts.note: Prussia was a German kingdom, abolished after 1918

explanation.surface: The head of an old monarchy abandons his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' names the first letter, P, and 'leaves' removes it from PRUSSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest nation in the world, spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Magical quality beginning to inspire Democrat (American)

indicators.note: to inspire means to breathe in, so the start takes in the other letters

parts.note: beginning means start
US means American

explanation.surface: A captivating aura is the seed of inspiration for an American Democrat politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is the enchanting, romantic glamour some people or things seem to carry about them.

clue.text: Trap cluster of French submarines in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
cluster of means a group of adjacent letters drawn out of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of French submarines falls back into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Trap cluster' as the definition, but only 'Trap' defines; 'cluster of' marks a run of letters inside 'French submarines', and 'in retreat' reverses HSUBMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from a hidden position, a trap laid for an enemy.

clue.text: Wrong clothing, say, for Muslim woman

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the wrong word encloses the example letters

parts.note: bum means bad or wrong, as in a bum note
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Someone asks if wearing the wrong clothes is acceptable for a Muslim woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A begum is a title for a high-ranking Muslim woman in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a South Asian honorific for a Muslim lady of rank, like a princess or noblewoman.

clue.text: With help, Solent sorted out a similar place in Turkey

indicators.note: sorted out means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting help to sort out the Solent, then visiting a Turkish counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England; 'similar place' asks for another strait, the Dardanelles' classical name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is a strait, so a similar place is the narrow strait in Turkey linking the Aegean and Marmara.

clue.text: Miss large outfit heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A young lady in an oversized outfit travels west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' turns LRIG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title used for an unmarried young woman, so it stands for a lass.

clue.text: Two bitters, one sent back in major face-off

parts.note: two words for bitter weather; the first is cold

indicators.note: sent back means that second word is returned, reading right to left

parts.note: one is the other of the two words for bitter weather, raw

explanation.surface: A drinker sends back one of two pints of bitter in a heated stand-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitters' looks like beers; it is two adjectives for chilly weather, COLD and RAW, and 'one sent back' reverses RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The postwar stand-off between the US and USSR was a long tense confrontation without open fighting.

clue.text: Collins, for one, is funnier after OED's tip

indicators.note: after means the stranger word follows the tip letter
tip here means the end letter of the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: rummer means odder, stranger, in British usage

explanation.surface: Collins, a rival dictionary, is supposedly funnier than the OED.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collins' looks like the Collins dictionary beside the OED; it is Phil Collins, drummer with Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Phil Collins played drums for the band Genesis before singing lead, an example of a percussionist.
